Also posted as arXiv:2504.07100 and reviewed on OpenReview (id: C7Mwox3C1u).

What EnDive is --------------- EnDive translates twelve widely-used English NLU / reasoning / coding / math benchmarks from Standard American English (SAE) into five underrepresented English dialects, using few-shot prompting with native-speaker-verified example translations, then validates the translations for fidelity.
The paper's own framing: the benchmark exists to measure whether large language models perform and behave fairly across dialects they were not primarily trained on, rather than only on SAE.

spans.text: That is 13 individual per-task HuggingFace dataset repositories, plus one combined repository (`EnDive_All_Datasets`) that — per its own file listing — holds only per-dialect `filtered_bleu_scores.csv` BLEU-score files for each task/dialect pair, not the translated text bodies themselves (those live in the 13 per-task repos).

Twelve of the thirteen per-task repos (all except NovelHopQA) share one schema, confirmed directly from each repo's own `dataset_info` metadata: five splits named exactly `AAVE`, `IndE`, `JamE`, `CollSgE`, `ChcE`, each row carrying (per BoolQ's own feature list, representative of the others): - "SAE Passage" (string) — the original Standard American English source - "SAE Question" (string) or task-equivalent field - "Actual Label" (task-appropriate type) - "Dialect (SAE Passage)" (string) — which dialect this row was translated into - "BLEU Score SAE Passage" (float64) — the paper's own automatic fidelity check for the translation
